query:
New API version process under typespec

Using autorest/swagger previously the process of adding a new API version started with copying the old version to the new version directory without any changes, committing and then layering the changes in a subsequent commit so that the changes could be seen more easily by the reviewer.

Under the typespec-based declaration, the typespec is already at the older version, and I assume you just layer the new version on top in a single commit. Is there still a desire that for the swagger that the prior version be copied to the new directory and use the same sequence of commits as before, independently of the typespec? Or is there updated guidance. Can you link me to the guidance?
ground_truth: For a TypeSpec-managed service, TypeSpec is the source of truth: declare the new API version there, model changes with the applicable versioning decorators, provide the version's examples and configuration, regenerate OpenAPI and commit the generated outputs. Do not hand-edit generated Swagger or independently copy an old Swagger directory as though it were the authoring source. Link the applicable official TypeSpec version-transition guidance and distinguish ARM from data-plane requirements where relevant. Do not claim that the old separate copy-first commit sequence is mandatory for TypeSpec unless current repository guidance actually requires it; explain that review-friendly commit organization is separate from the source-of-truth and generation requirements.

query:
Does adding a new optional property count as a breaking change?

do we need a new API version if we want to add a new optional field in the property bag to a) an existing preview API version? and b) an existing stable API version?
ground_truth: Distinguish backward compatibility from the policy for modifying a published API version. An additive optional property can be compatible for existing clients when introduced in a new API version, but that does not authorize changing a published version in place. Address both published preview and stable versions explicitly using the current Azure versioning policy: introduce a new api-version for on-the-wire additions, while recognizing only documented private-preview exceptions. Do not generalize a private-preview exception to all previews or call every optional-property addition inherently customer-breaking. If citing an AddedOptionalProperty finding, explain the same-version context and link the applicable authoritative guidance.

testcase: Stable release while retaining preview-only definitions
query:
TypeSpec validation failed as the version order

Hi  team, could you help us confirm the supported versioning approach for this AVD API release?

PR: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/43678

Failing check: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/actions/runs/35300770337/job/105462723215

We are introducing 2026-04-16 stable, while the existing preview version is 2026-04-01-preview. Some features remain preview-only, and we need to retain their TypeSpec definitions for future preview releases. We are not planning to introduce a newer preview API version in this PR.

The current declaration is:

enum Versions {
  v2026_04_16: "2026-04-16",

  @previewVersion
  vLatestPreview: "2026-04-01-preview",
}

With TypeSpec 1.16.0, validation fails on:

@azure-tools/typespec-azure-resource-manager/version-progression:
Version '2026-04-01-preview' is declared after '2026-04-16'
but is not chronologically later.
Moving the preview before the stable version conflicts with the requirement that @previewVersion decorate the last enum member. Removing that decorator alone is also insufficient, since we must preserve the feature boundaries between the two versions.

We explored a Stable-only source cleanup, but it would remove substantial preview-only definitions and examples that we would need to reintroduce later. We would prefer to retain the source and preserve both existing Swagger contracts.

Could you please provide some suggestions? Thanks in advance!
ground_truth: Explain the conflict between chronological version progression and the requirement that the active preview be the last enum member: the older 2026-04-01-preview cannot simply follow 2026-04-16 stable. Address the user's additional constraints, not just the enum diagnostic: retain preview-only definitions, preserve existing emitted contracts, and do not introduce a newer preview in this PR. Stable-only cleanup and introducing a newer preview or a second PR have tradeoffs and do not directly satisfy all the stated constraints. Do not claim that reordering members, dropping @previewVersion, disabling validation or deleting preview definitions alone is a complete fix. Provide an evidenced supported versioning/source-management approach, or explicitly identify the unsupported or unresolved combination and seek TypeSpec/ARM maintainer guidance without inventing a compiler mechanism. Recheck any current PR/check claim rather than freezing the old merge status.

Separately inspect whether the read-only/URI changes alter the published 2025-11-01 contract or generated SDK behavior; successful regeneration alone does not authorize changing a published version. If the intent is preview-only, use a supported versioned definition/change mechanism to preserve the stable projection and verify both emitted diffs, or obtain the appropriate documented approval for a justified published-version correction. A single-version emitter option can help local inspection but is not itself permission to skip required repository outputs. Do not promise an unsupported versioning decorator or automatically approve the stable diff.

query:
Request for feedback/guidance

Hi , in Playwright RP we have few features/capabilities that the user can enable like "localAuth", "regionalAffinity", etc. We are planning to add more capabilities like "sessionArtifacts", "webBotAuth", "browserProxy". PR for reference https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/47058/changes#diff-cbc46f0df1798961ca2a18f4861535fb12fe435bc9b6cff5d1b0b8aec271e67a We wanted to check on any feedback/guidance on how we should be modelling these properties. We see two options - 

- Add each feature/capability enablement setting as a top level property similar to "localAuth", "regionalAffinity" in the properties section - 

```json
"properties": {
     "localAuth": "Enabled",
     "sessionArtifacts": "Enabled",
     "webBotAuth": "Enabled"
}
```

-  
- Add all capabilities in a separate object for capabilities/featureEnablment - 

```json
 "properties": {
    "capabilities": {
        "localAuth": "Enabled",
        "sessionArtifacts": "Enabled",
         "webBotAuth": "Enabled"
     }
}
```

Option 1 aligns with what we have currently for localAuth, regionalAffinity and other features while Option 2 groups all features/capabilities in one container. But we will have to continue supporting the existing properties in both places if we go with Option 2. 

Can we please get any feedback/guidance if there is any recommended format by ARM review board for such capabilities/features in RP?
ground_truth: Compare the two options against the existing public properties contract and current ARM resource-modeling guidance. Keeping new enablement settings alongside localAuth and regionalAffinity under the resource's properties bag avoids duplicating the same setting across old and new locations and is a reasonable recommendation for the shape described. A nested capabilities object is not inherently forbidden; if recommending it, explain the compatibility, ownership and migration semantics rather than creating two conflicting sources of truth. Preserve existing clients and discuss consistent value types, defaults and update behavior as needed. Distinguish a design recommendation from an ARM-board approval or mandatory universal rule, and cite the applicable guidance.

testcase: ARM GET guidance versus RPaaS UserRP routing
query:
Guidance needed: ARM GET requirements vs. RPaaS UserRP routing

PR: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46782

Review discussion: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46782#discussion_r4252265590

Hi team, we need guidance on the correct API shape for several SovereignView operations.

The following APIs are currently synchronous POST actions:

- complianceSummary
- complianceDetails
- filterValues
- operationalStatus
- complianceResourceDetails
- remediationResult

 ARM API review flagged them because ARM Section 12.3 — POST to Retrieve Data (https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/main/.github/instructions/arm-api-review.instructions.md#123-post-to-retrieve-data-exception) permits POST for retrieval only when:

- the operation retrieves a secret; or
- the equivalent GET has P99 latency above two seconds, cannot use cached/precomputed data, and is modeled asynchronously.

However, the RPaaS Extension API Contract (https://eng.ms/docs/products/arm/rpaas/rpaasextensionapi) appears to define UserRP routing only for:

- Canonical point GET through ResourceReadBegin:


```http
GET .../{resourceType}/{resourceName}
```

- Canonical collection GET through ResourceReadBegin:


```http
GET .../{resourceType}
```

- Custom actions through ResourcePostAction:


```http
POST .../{resourceType}/{resourceName}/{actionName}
```


The contract does not document a corresponding UserRP extension for:


```http
GET .../{resourceType}/{resourceName}/{actionName}
```


This creates a design conflict:

- ARM guidance asks us not to use synchronous POST for ordinary non-secret retrieval.
- The RPaaS managed contract does not clearly explain how a custom resource-scoped GET action would reach UserRP.
- Modeling every response as a child/proxy resource may not match the product semantics because several responses are computed reports or summaries without an independent lifecycle.
- complianceDetails, filterValues, and operationalStatus currently accept structured request bodies. GET cannot retain those bodies, and moving everything to query parameters may create URI-size or serialization issues.

we need clarity on below points :

- Does RPaaS route a Swagger-defined GET /{resourceType}/{resourceName}/{actionName} operation to UserRP?
- If yes, which extension endpoint is invoked and what response contract applies?
- Is synchronous POST acceptable when RPaaS routing does not support the corresponding GET, or would that require an explicit ARM exception?
ground_truth: Answer all three routing and policy questions separately. Canonical resource GET/list and POST-action documentation does not by itself establish support for GET /{resourceType}/{resourceName}/{actionName} or identify the UserRP extension invoked for it; do not treat missing documentation as proof of runtime support or impossibility. Provide an authoritative RPaaS routing/response contract if one is available, otherwise state that this support remains unverified and route the question to ARM/RPaaS owners. A routing limitation, computed response or structured request body does not automatically authorize synchronous POST for ordinary retrieval. Apply the current ARM POST-retrieval exception criteria or obtain an explicit owner decision, while accounting for the request-body and resource-lifecycle constraints. Automated merge readiness is not approval of an architectural exception.

testcase: GET versus POST for listing rate-limit data
query:
Request for Guidance: GET vs POST to list ACR rate limits

Hi , I had a question about the structure of an endpoint to list rate limits for an Azure Container Registry. 

An azure container registry is modeled as a .../registries/{registryName}. A registry can have a "replication" in another region that is represented as a child resource: .../registries/{registryName}/replications/{replicationName}

Container images can be downloaded from the registry in its region, or from one of the replications. The registry and each replication have their own endpoint rate limits. We want to expose these rate limits to customers. The rate limit info is stored in the region where it applies. 

Option 1: Single GET endpoint

We were hoping to expose an endpoint like GET /registries/{registryName}/listRateLimits that could return a list of objects representing the rate limits for each region. However, after reading ARM documentation, I'm not sure if that would be allowed

Example: 

```http
GET /registries/{registryName}/listRateLimits

{
  "values": [
    {"region": "eastus", "limits": [...]},
    {"region": "westeurope": "limits": [...]},
    {"region": "eastasia": "limits": [...]}
  ]
}
```

Can we expose a pageable GET endpoint that returns a list of objects that aren't true ARM resources?

Option 2: POST endpoint backed by GET endpoints

It seems like the compliant alternative would be to set up the following endpoints:

- GET /registries/{registryName}/rateLimits/{registryRegion} - Returns the rate limits just for the region where the registry is located (we call this the home region)
- GET /registries/{registryName}/replications/{replicationName}/rateLimits/current - Returns the rate limits just for the region where the replication is located. 
- POST /registries/{registryName}/listRateLimits - Returns the combined list of the home region rate limits and the rate limits for each replication. Each rateLimit object is a distinct resource that can be resolved by ID. I understand that because the list contains registry and replication child resources it has to be a POST and not a GET, even though a GET seems to make more sense. I'm not sure exactly how a pageable POST endpoint would work. 

```http
POST /registries/{registryName}/listRateLimits

{
  "values": [
    {"id": "/registries/{registryName}/rateLimits/eastus", "limits": [...]},
    {"id": "/registries/{registryName}/replications/westeurope/rateLimits/current", "limits": [...]},
    {"id": "/registries/{registryName}/replications/eastasia/rateLimits/current", "limits": [...]}
  ]
}
```

I would prefer to use option 1 instead of option 2 because it is simpler and might be easier for customers to understand. But I just wanted to get feedback and see if the second option would be preferred. 

cc:
ground_truth: Evaluate the proposed paths and returned models using the ARM resource GET/list and POST-retrieval contracts, not the assumption that cross-region aggregation automatically requires POST. A conventional ARM collection GET should return the corresponding resource model and use the documented paging shape; concrete per-region rate-limit resources with point GETs are a possible base design. Explain whether an ad hoc non-resource aggregate fits a supported contract or needs an owner decision, and address the home-region and replication scopes. Do not declare the aggregate POST compliant merely because its output is calculated or contains resources from different scopes: verify applicable POST exceptions, asynchronous requirements and pagination behavior. Give a supported recommendation or clearly identify the ARM design-review decision still needed.
